message:
We’ll build an IBM Cloud invoice workflow that extracts the four fields, queues them for review and prevents repeat deliveries from creating duplicate invoices. Let’s use one composed application with durable processing and approval records; accounting compatibility and regional availability still need verification.

**Which country must this system’s invoices and processing stay in?** This determines placement; for example, “Australia”, “no restriction” or “not sure”.

followUp.question: Which country must this system’s invoices and processing stay in?
followUp.why: This determines placement of invoice storage, extraction and recovery data, and whether the existing accounting destination fits that boundary.
followUp.example: Australia; no restriction; or not sure.

proposal.title: IBM invoice intake, review and approved delivery
proposal.body: Propose PDF upload, extraction, staff review and approved accounting submission as the initial scope. Automatic approval, payments and non-invoice processing are outside this proposed first version. Use the supported composed invoice-workflow module; its internal resources are described within the application rather than duplicated. Country and region remain undecided. Accounting API compatibility, destination identities, model policy, recovery and deployed behavior require independent acceptance evidence.

next.name: Asynchronous document intake
next.requirements: Users upload PDF invoices. Extract the supplier, invoice date, total and currency into a review queue. Delivery can repeat; retries must not create duplicate invoices. A reviewer approves a result before it is sent to our existing accounting API. Use IBM Cloud. Recommend a coherent system and the engineering choices. Ask only a small material business question when needed; do not make me configure the system.

data.label: Invoice uploaders and reviewers
data.description: Existing people using a browser, outside provisioning scope. Upload PDF invoices, inspect extracted fields and source evidence, correct results and approve an exact result revision. Proposed application permissions distinguish upload and reviewer access; actual staff enrollment remains a destination input.

data.label: Invoice intake and approval
data.description: Proposed composed deployment on IBM Code Engine owns browser/API, background worker, isolated PDF/OCR parser and operating tasks. Internal managed resources include IBM Cloud Databases for PostgreSQL for transactional work queue, review state, approval records and delivery outbox; private versioned IBM Cloud Object Storage for originals; staff sign-in and reviewer membership; and regional watsonx extraction with supplier, invoice date, total, currency and source evidence. Parser receives untrusted PDF bytes without database, accounting or model credentials. Separate workload identities and server-side authorization protect each responsibility. Durable intake identity and source fingerprints handle repeated delivery; approval binds the exact result revision and destination contract. Accounting submissions retain one operation ID and payload identity across bounded retries. Uncertain outcomes are held for reconciliation rather than blindly resent. Owns retention, monitoring, audit and restore procedures. Proposed reviewable defaults: 10 MB PDFs, 100 pages and 90-day retention eligibility, subject to backup/version review. This module owns its internal services; no separate duplicate nodes are needed. Regional support, staff identity configuration, model policy, accounting contract and combined runtime behavior remain unverified.

config.region: To be selected after country decision

data.label: Existing accounting API
data.description: Client-owned existing accounting service, referenced without recreation or modification. Receives only approved invoice revisions through the guarded accounting adapter. Native API compatibility is not established: an adapter must independently pass normalized-action-v1 and durable idempotency acceptance, including timeout reconciliation. Endpoint, authorization and actual processing location require destination review; no credentials are stored in the diagram.

edges.label: HTTPS: upload PDF, review evidence, approve; receive status
HTTPS: approved invoice with stable operation ID; receipt or reconciliation

requirementDrafts.rationale: Makes extraction useful and inspectable while preventing uncertain or invalid model output from silently progressing.
requirementDrafts.basis: “Users upload PDF invoices. Extract the supplier, invoice date, total and currency into a review queue.” Source evidence and explicit failure states are proposed safeguards.
requirementDrafts.statement: Accept PDF invoice uploads and durably queue extraction of supplier, invoice date, total and currency for staff review. Proposed safeguards retain source evidence and expose invalid, uncertain or failed extraction for correction without accounting submission.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Prevents automated or stale approvals from authorizing accounting changes.
requirementDrafts.basis: “A reviewer approves a result before it is sent to our existing accounting API.” Revision binding and server-side reviewer authorization are proposed enforcement choices.
requirementDrafts.statement: Require an authorized reviewer’s approval of the exact invoice result revision before accounting submission. Editing the approved fields invalidates that approval; extraction output and uploader-supplied claims cannot authorize delivery.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Repeated delivery and lost accounting responses can otherwise create duplicate financial records. End-to-end assurance depends on the destination’s independently tested idempotency and reconciliation behavior.
requirementDrafts.basis: “Delivery can repeat; retries must not create duplicate invoices.” Durable operation identity, bounded retries and uncertain-outcome reconciliation are proposed engineering controls.
requirementDrafts.statement: Repeated intake delivery and processing or accounting retries must not create duplicate invoices. Persist intake and delivery identities, preserve the same operation and payload identity on replay, and hold uncertain accounting outcomes for reconciliation. Acceptance must include duplicate delivery, worker restart and timeout-after-destination-commit cases.

skills.name: Architecture composition and engineering judgment
skills.summary: Choose and compose blocks through responsibility, contracts, state, identity, failure modes and trade-offs; verify the complete system.
skills.source: AtMem AI Architect reviewed specialist guidance

skills.name: AI architecture and discovery
skills.summary: Clarify outcome, users, existing systems, data ownership and constraints. Evolve the diagram incrementally. Derive functional requirements and propose measurable quality targets as assumptions needing confirmation. Compare clouds against the actual requirements; do not assume an enterprise identity provider or a vendor. Keep proposed and accepted decisions distinct.
skills.source: AtMem AI Architect reviewed specialist guidance

skills.name: IBM Cloud architecture guidance
skills.summary: Match watsonx, data services, identity, application runtime and observability to the same requirements used for other clouds. Check region, data residency, model access and IBM plan before pricing. Use a sourced IBM quote; do not substitute an AWS/Azure rate or claim an unsupported deployment is ready.
